attributes.action: When Justice Fails: Reform Sentencing, Prison and the Pursuit of Fairness
attributes.additional_details: This petition calls for urgent reform of England and Wales’s criminal justice system. It challenges racial and religious disparities in conviction, sentencing and prison discipline, questions inconsistencies where intention can outweigh actual harm, and exposes how punitive custody can fuel reoffending. We demand evidence based sentencing, transparency, proportionality and rehabilitation that protects the public while restoring confidence in justice.
attributes.background: We call on Parliament to independently review sentencing and prison practice, enforce transparency over racial and religious disparities, reassess disproportionate sentences, and prioritise evidence based rehabilitation to uphold equality, proportionality and public safety.

rejection.details:
We aren't clear as to what exactly you are calling for.  The Government has recently undertaken a review of sentencing:
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/independent-sentencing-review-final-report

We also can't publish petitions when the request is something that's already happening (or something that has been announced since you started your petition).  Parliament does regularly scrutinise the things you refer to - through Oral Questions and Written Questions, debates in the Chamber and Westminster Hall and the work of the Justice Select Committee, for example:

https://committees.parliament.uk/committee/102/justice-committee

We think a lot of your petition is covered by Government or Parliament action already. If you'd like something else, you could start a new petition clearly explaining what it is.
